title: Turning the Tables
text: “This is starting to sound interesting. Iwatani-sama, whatever did you come up with?”

“Theo, hold yourself back a bit, would you? If you go rampaging too hard, I won’t be able to get my payback in. I was thinking this whole upcoming mess was going to be a pain, so I figured I’d liven it up a little.”
“Depending on the details, I understand.”
“Alright then, Shion, let’s head back to the venue. If this goes well, we can free her through perfectly legal means.”
The mongrel lizardman fell into a silence that could only be described as somewhat exasperated.
“W-what are you planning to do!? Hey! Ngh……”

Éclair looked more worn out than the one I remembered. Being tortured and locked away had clearly weakened her. If I did too many good deeds I’d end up dying, so I’d been holding myself back, I say. Was it that, perhaps? There was more than a zero chance that shipping the Three Heroes Church lot off to Siltvelt had led to an increase in torture. In that sense, securing Éclair now wasn’t a bad move at all. More importantly, in none of the previous loops had I ever managed to bring Éclair onto our side at this particular timing, so it fit perfectly with my goal of doing all sorts of new things, indeed.
“Motoyasu-kun, let’s head back to the venue while concealed. If they’re moving around to pick a fight, they must be searching high and low for me since I’m not there.”
“Leave it to me, I say.”
And so, Father hurried us back toward the venue. Along the way, soldiers and other assorted types were dashing all over the castle grounds.
“Hurry and bring out the next dish!”

They seemed frantic to pinpoint Father’s location so they could pick a fight with him. Repulsive lot, I say. The rabbit man seemed to have caught on too, his brow furrowing. Once we got back to the venue, we casually slipped in from a corner of the garden, pretending we’d just strolled back in.

Then Father raised a hand slightly to signal us to keep our distance, before walking off toward the table lined with food. And right on cue, as if lying in wait, the Crimson Swine appeared and approached him, timed just so. This flow felt similar to the time I’d roped Ren into playing along. Incidentally, Ren, still apparently feeling queasy, was lying across some connected chairs.
“Shadow Saint, still not eating?”
“Ugh……”
Right in front of Ren, Kuro-chan was munching away happily. The other Filolial-samas were eating plenty too. I do so love it when everyone eats a lot, I say!
“Here, these pitch-black claws and fangs brought you food, so eat up and stock up on your dark power~”
What a heartwarming sight. A moment of healing before having to lay eyes on that unpleasant creature, the Crimson Swine, trying to latch onto Father.
Father cast a scornful glance at the approaching Crimson Swine while pretending to focus on the food on the table, feigning indifference.
“BWEEEEEEHHH! Bwoink! Bwee-bwee-bwee-BWEEEEE!”
And here, the Crimson Swine let out an extremely contrived shriek.
“……what on earth is that farce? Screeching like that after approaching on its own.”
“I do wonder about being screamed at this blatantly. This is what they mean by being lost for words. Did you see that? It had the look of someone who’d just found their weapon of choice.”

The mongrel lizardman and the rabbit man were staring at the Crimson Swine with expressions that had gone past mere exasperation into something else entirely. It’d been a while, hadn’t it, Crimson Swine…… How should I dispose of it this loop, I wonder? If possible, I’d like to make it suffer. I still hadn’t forgotten the grudge on behalf of Fleon-chan from the very first world. That reminds me—shipping it off to the Pig King as-is, letting it spend its days in terror on that island alongside Takt, sounded like fun too. But since Father seemed to have a plan, I’d let it slide this time, I say.
“Haaaaaaaaah……”
Father let out an exceedingly deep sigh at the Crimson Swine clinging to him. Then he resolved to completely ignore it and gently stroked a nearby Filolial-sama who was busy eating.
“BWEE! Bwee-bwee-bwee! BWEEEH!”

Faced with Father’s decision to ignore it entirely, the Crimson Swine only heated up further. Under normal circumstances, that filthy squealing would just be unpleasant, but knowing Father had a plan made it all rather exciting.
“Iwatani-sama really doesn’t hold back, does he. That should make it obvious at a glance who’s in the right.”
“What exactly are you planning?”
“Bwee! Bwee-bwee-bwee! BWEEEEHHH!”

Sensing the wind was blowing the wrong way, the Crimson Swine let out a squeal, and Father, along with the mongrel lizardman, the rabbit man, and even the Filolial-samas, all made faces of displeasure.
The booing of the Filolial-samas rang out. What had it said, I wonder? Apparently it had gone so far as to say things like hanging criminals or cutting down the Filolials right there.
“Bwee-bwee……”

The Crimson Swine, trying to seek help from Ren, noticed he was far too limp to be of any use and swept its beady eyes around at the other heroes nearby. What a repulsive gaze. The gaze of someone skilled at making disgusting excuses, scanning its surroundings for material to defend itself with. It seemed to have intended to use Ren as leverage, to reinforce whichever side—the kingdom or Father—was supposedly in the right. I’d seen this before, but even Ren back then had worn an expression practically screaming why do I have to fight? When Father had been more unstable, provoking him there had made things escalate, but the current Father wouldn’t do such a thing. After all, he held a favorable impression of Ren now, given how close he was with Kuro-chan.
“Just what is all this commotion about?”
“BWEEEEEE! Bwee-bwee-bwee! Bwee-bwoink!”
As if it had finally found its mark, the Crimson Swine dashed over to Itsuki and hid behind him, squealing about something. Now then, Itsuki, how will you respond, I wonder?
“I see…… Naofumi-san. So you said something hurtful again, right after reuniting with Princess Malty.”

The Crimson Swine had apparently seized the moment to spread more lies to Itsuki. Itsuki looked displeased. Likewise, Father, along with the mongrel lizardman and the rabbit man, all wore looks of exasperation. Before long, Father let out a faint chuckle and opened his mouth as if to provoke.
“……Itsuki, what did you think, hearing that?”

Playing the victim here would’ve been easy enough, and Itsuki wasn’t quite foolish enough for that, but it seemed he’d chosen a response that hinted it would make resolving Éclair’s problem more difficult. In other words, he’d chosen to provoke.

I see! Now I understood everything. In other words, he was turning the very same acts that the Crimson Swine, Trash, and even I myself had committed in the very first world back on them, using it to spring a trap! Well done, Father, I say.
Falling perfectly for the provocation, Itsuki drew his bow and took aim.
“I was still in the process of grasping the full situation, but now you’ve shown your true colors!”
Itsuki wore the look of someone thoroughly convinced. An extremely irritating expression, I say. Ah yes, this was starting to resemble the flow of the loop where I’d stayed behind in Melromarc.

“Enslaving people and forcing them into battles they don’t even want to fight, making them fight to the death—this is beneath even the lowest of heroes! And on top of that, twisting the knife in the wounds of a woman you yourself hurt…… Release them this instant! Or I won’t forgive you!”
Itsuki, do you want to save the Crimson Swine, or do you want to abolish the slavery system? Which is it, I wonder? Wanting both at once seemed just a touch greedy.
“Oh my, well then——”

At that point, the rabbit man, looking displeased, was about to step forward, but Father silently pressured him to stop. Reluctantly, the rabbit man backed down. Apparently, if the rabbit man and Itsuki got into an argument, Itsuki’s attention might drift and the situation could veer off from the intended course, hence the warning. Later, the rabbit man would grumble under his breath that even though he understood the reasoning, he still hadn’t liked it one bit.
